card.name: Words leading into adverse-event outcome terms
card.fires_on: Words just before an expected outcome term in adverse-event or trial-endpoint text, such as 'permanent' before discontinuation, 'end' before stage renal disease, or 'agic' in hemorrhagic.

modes.label: Permanent before discontinuation
modes.description: The word 'permanent' after 'resulted in' or 'led to', ahead of 'discontinuation'.
modes.example: Events resolved in 4 of the 9 patients and resulted in<< permanent>> discontinuation in 1 patient.

modes.label: Hemorrhagic events
modes.description: The ending 'agic' of hemorrhagic, in incidence statements about bleeding events or stroke.
modes.example: the incidence of any grade hemorrh<<agic>> events during the entire treatment period was

modes.label: Start of a set endpoint phrase
modes.description: A word opening a fixed clinical phrase, such as 'end' before stage renal disease or 'wound' before healing complications.
modes.example: decline in GFR,<< end>> state renal disease, or death, but
